sentences.en: As the world begins to experiment with the power of artificial intelligence, a debate has begun about how to contain its risks.
sentences.zh: 随着世界开始尝试人工智能的力量，关于如何遏制其风险的辩论已经开始。

sentences.en: One of the sharpest and most urgent warnings has come from the man who helped invent the technology.
sentences.zh: 最尖锐、最紧迫的警告之一来自这位帮助发明了该技术的人。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Cade Metz speaks to Jeffrey Hinton, who many consider to be the godfather of AI.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事凯德·梅茨采访了杰弗里·辛顿，许多人认为他是人工智能的教父。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, May 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月30日，星期二。

sentences.en: Cade, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 凯德，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Glad to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So a few weeks ago, you interviewed Jeffrey Hinton, a man who many people know as the godfather of AI.
sentences.zh: 几周前，你采访了杰弗里·辛顿，许多人称他为人工智能教父。

sentences.en: And aside from the obvious fact that AI is really taking over all conversations at all times, why talk to Jeff now?
sentences.zh: 除了人工智能确实在时刻占据所有话题这一显而易见的事实外，为什么现在要采访杰夫？

sentences.en: I've known Jeff a long time.
sentences.zh: 我认识杰夫很久了。

sentences.en: I wrote a book about the 50-year rise of the ideas that are now driving chatbots like ChatGPT and Google Bard.
sentences.zh: 我写过一本书，讲述了那些如今驱动ChatGPT和谷歌Bard等聊天机器人的思想，它们经历了50年的发展历程。

sentences.en: And you could argue that he is the most important person to the rise of AI over the past 50 years.
sentences.zh: 你可以说他是过去50年人工智能崛起中最重要的人物。

sentences.en: And amidst all this that's happening with these chatbots, he sent me an email and said,
sentences.zh: 在这些聊天机器人引发的所有事件中，他给我发了一封电子邮件，说：

sentences.en: I'm leaving Google and I want to talk to you and that he wants to discuss where this technology is going, including some serious concerns.
sentences.zh: 我要离开谷歌了，我想和你谈谈，他想讨论这项技术的发展方向，包括一些严重的担忧。

sentences.en: Who better to talk to than the godfather of AI?
sentences.zh: 还有谁比人工智能教父更适合交谈呢？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So naturally, I got on a plane and I went to Toronto.
sentences.zh: 所以很自然地，我坐上飞机去了多伦多。

sentences.en: Jeff.
sentences.zh: 杰夫。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 来吧。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 来吧。

sentences.en: It's great to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: To sit down at his dinner table and discuss.
sentences.zh: 坐在他的餐桌旁进行讨论。

sentences.en: Would you like a cup of coffee, a cup of tea, a beer, some whiskey?
sentences.zh: 你想喝杯咖啡、茶、啤酒还是威士忌？

sentences.en: If you've made some coffee.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经煮了咖啡的话。

sentences.en: Jeff is a 75-year-old Cambridge-educated British man who now lives in Toronto.
sentences.zh: 杰夫是一位75岁、在剑桥受过教育的英国人，现在住在多伦多。

sentences.en: He's been there since the late 80s.
sentences.zh: 他从80年代末就一直住在那里。

sentences.en: He's a professor at the university.
sentences.zh: 他是大学教授。

sentences.en: My question is, somewhere along the way, people started calling you the godfather of AI.
sentences.zh: 我的问题是，在某个阶段，人们开始称你为人工智能教父。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure it was meant as a compliment.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这是否是赞美。

sentences.en: And do AI researchers come to your door and kneel before you and kiss your hand?
sentences.zh: 人工智能研究人员会来到你家门口，跪在你面前亲吻你的手吗？

sentences.en: Like, how does it work?
sentences.zh: 比如，这是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: Like, no, no, they don't.
sentences.zh: 不，不，他们不会。

sentences.en: They don't.
sentences.zh: 他们不会。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: And I never get to ask them for favors.
sentences.zh: 而且我从不要求他们帮我什么忙。

sentences.en: So how does Jeff become the godfather of AI?
sentences.zh: 那么杰夫是如何成为人工智能教父的？

sentences.en: Where does his story start?
sentences.zh: 他的故事从哪里开始？

sentences.en: It starts in high school.
sentences.zh: 从高中开始。

sentences.en: He grew up the son of an academic, but he always tells a story about a friend describing a theory of how the brain works.
sentences.zh: 他是一位学者的儿子，但他总是讲一个朋友描述大脑工作原理理论的故事。

sentences.en: And he wrote about holograms, and he got interested in the idea that memory in the brain might be like a hologram.
sentences.zh: 他写过关于全息图的文章，并对大脑记忆可能像全息图的想法产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: This friend talked about the way the brain stores memories.
sentences.zh: 这位朋友谈到了大脑存储记忆的方式。

sentences.en: And that he felt it stored these memories like a hologram.
sentences.zh: 他觉得大脑像全息图一样存储这些记忆。

sentences.en: A hologram isn't stored in a single spot.
sentences.zh: 全息图不是存储在单一位置的。

sentences.en: It's divided into tiny pieces and then spread across a piece of film.
sentences.zh: 它被分成微小的碎片，然后分布在一片胶片上。

sentences.en: And this friend felt that the brain stored memories in the same way, that it broke these memories into pieces and stored them across the network of neurons in the brain.
sentences.zh: 这位朋友认为大脑以同样的方式存储记忆，它将这些记忆分解成碎片，并存储在大脑的神经元网络中。

sentences.en: It's quite beautiful, actually.
sentences.zh: 这其实很美。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And we talked about that.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论过那个。

sentences.en: And I've been interested in how the brain worked ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，我就一直对大脑的工作原理很感兴趣。

sentences.en: That sparked Jeff's intereSt.
sentences.zh: 那激发了杰夫的兴趣。

sentences.en: And from there on, he spent his life in pursuit of trying to understand how the brain worked.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他终其一生都在追求了解大脑是如何工作的。

sentences.en: So how does Jeff start to answer the question of how the brain works?
sentences.zh: 那么杰夫是如何开始回答大脑如何工作这个问题的呢？

sentences.en: So he goes to Cambridge, and he studies physiology, looking for answers from his professors.
sentences.zh: 他去了剑桥，学习生理学，从教授那里寻找答案。

sentences.en: Can you tell me how the brain works?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我大脑是如何工作的吗？

sentences.en: And his physiology professors can't tell him.
sentences.zh: 他的生理学教授无法告诉他。

sentences.en: And so I switched to philosophy, and then I switched to psychology, in the hopes that psychology would tell me more about the mind.
sentences.zh: 所以我转到了哲学，然后转到了心理学，希望心理学能告诉我更多关于心灵的知识。

sentences.en: And it didn't.
sentences.zh: 但并没有。

sentences.en: And no one can tell him how the brain works.
sentences.zh: 没有人能告诉他大脑是如何工作的。

sentences.en: The layperson might ask, don't we understand how the brain works?
sentences.zh: 外行可能会问，我们难道不了解大脑是如何工作的吗？

sentences.en: No, we don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我们不了解。

sentences.en: We understand some things about how it works.
sentences.zh: 我们了解它工作方式的一些方面。

sentences.en: I mean, we understand that when you're thinking, or when you're perceiving, there's neurons, brain cells, and the brain cells fire.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们知道当你思考或感知时，会有神经元，即脑细胞，而脑细胞会放电。

sentences.en: They go ping, and send the ping along an axon to other brain cells.
sentences.zh: 它们发出信号，沿着轴突将信号发送给其他脑细胞。

sentences.en: We still don't know the details of how the neurons in our brains communicate with one another as we think and learn.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然不知道当我们思考和学习时，大脑中的神经元如何相互交流的细节。

sentences.en: And so all you need to know now is, well, how does it decide on the strengths of the connections between neurons?
sentences.zh: 所以你现在只需要知道，它是如何决定神经元之间连接强度的？

sentences.en: If you could figure that out, you understand how the brain works.
sentences.zh: 如果你能弄清楚这一点，你就了解大脑是如何工作的了。

sentences.en: And we haven't figured it out yet.
sentences.zh: 而我们还没有弄清楚。

sentences.en: He then moves into a relatively new field called artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 随后他进入了一个相对较新的领域，称为人工智能。

sentences.en: The field of artificial intelligence was created in the late 50s by a small group of scientists in the United States.
sentences.zh: 人工智能领域是由美国的一小群科学家在50年代末创建的。

sentences.en: Their aim was to create a machine that could do anything the human brain could do.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是创造一台能做人脑能做的任何事情的机器。

sentences.en: And in the beginning, many of them thought they could build machines that operated like the network of neurons in the brain, what they called artificial neural networks.
sentences.zh: 起初，他们中的许多人认为他们可以制造出像大脑神经元网络那样运作的机器，也就是他们所说的“人工神经网络”。

sentences.en: But 10 years into this work, progress was so slow that they assumed it was too difficult to
sentences.zh: 但在工作了10年后，进展非常缓慢，以至于他们认为制造一台像大脑神经元那样运作的机器太难了，

sentences.en: build a machine that operated like the neurons in the brain, and they gave up on the idea.
sentences.zh: 于是他们放弃了这个想法。

sentences.en: So they embraced a very different way of thinking about artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们接受了一种关于人工智能的截然不同的思考方式。

sentences.en: They embraced something they called symbolic AI.
sentences.zh: 他们接受了所谓的“符号人工智能”。

sentences.en: You would take everything that you and I know about the world and put them into a list of rules.
sentences.zh: 你会把你和我所知道的关于世界的一切都列入规则清单中。

sentences.en: Things like you can't be in two places at the same time, or when you hold a coffee cup, you hold the open end up.
sentences.zh: 比如你不能同时出现在两个地方，或者当你拿咖啡杯时，要保持开口向上。

sentences.en: The idea was that you would list all these rules step by step, line of code by line of code, and then feed that into a machine.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，你一步一步、一行代码一行代码地列出所有这些规则，然后输入到机器中。

sentences.en: And then that would give it the power that you and I have in our own brains.
sentences.zh: 然后这就会赋予它你我大脑中拥有的那种能力。

sentences.en: So essentially, tell the computer every rule that governs reality, and the computer makes the decisions based on all of those rules.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，告诉计算机支配现实的每一条规则，计算机就会根据所有这些规则做出决定。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But then Jeff Hinton comes along in 1972 as a graduate student in Edinburgh, and he says, wait, wait, wait, that is never going to happen.
sentences.zh: 但后来杰夫·辛顿在1972年作为爱丁堡的研究生出现了，他说，等等，等等，那永远不会发生。

sentences.en: That's a lot of rules.
sentences.zh: 那规则太多了。

sentences.en: You will never have the time and the patience and the person power to write all those rules and feed them into a machine.
sentences.zh: 你永远没有时间、耐心和人力去写下所有这些规则并把它们输入到机器里。

sentences.en: I don't care how long you take, he says, it is not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不在乎你花多长时间，这都不会发生。

sentences.en: And by the way, the human brain doesn't work like that.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，人脑不是那样工作的。

sentences.en: That's not how we learn.
sentences.zh: 我们不是那样学习的。

sentences.en: So he returns to the old idea of a neural network that was discarded earlier by other
sentences.zh: 所以他回到了之前被其他人工智能研究人员抛弃的神经网络的旧想法。

sentences.en: AI researchers.
sentences.zh: 他说，那才是我们应该用来构建思考机器的方法。

sentences.en: And he says, that is the way that we should build machines that think.
sentences.zh: 我们要让它们像人类学习那样从世界中学习。

sentences.en: We have them learn from the world like humans learn.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其像其他人那样给计算机输入一堆规则，不如给它输入一堆信息。

sentences.en: So instead of feeding the computer a bunch of rules, like the other guys were doing, you'd actually feed it a bunch of information.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，计算机将逐渐理清如何理解这一切，就像人脑一样。

sentences.en: And the idea was that the computer would gradually sort out how to make sense of it all, like a human brain.
sentences.zh: 你会给它提供世界上正在发生的事情的例子，它会分析这些例子，寻找世界上所发生事情的模式，并从这些模式中学习。

sentences.en: You would give it examples of what is happening in the world, and it would analyze those examples and look for patterns in what happens in the world and learn from those patterns.
sentences.zh: 但杰夫正在采纳一个在很大程度上已被大多数人工智能社区抛弃的想法。

sentences.en: But Jeff is taking up an idea that had been largely discarded by the majority of the AI community.
sentences.zh: 他有任何证据表明他的方法真的会奏效吗？

sentences.en: Did he have any evidence that his approach was actually going to work?
sentences.zh: 相信它可能奏效的唯一理由是因为大脑确实在工作。

sentences.en: The only reason to believe it might work at all was because the brain works.
sentences.zh: 这是相信还有任何希望的主要原因。

sentences.en: And that was the main reason for believing there was any hope at all.
sentences.zh: 他唯一的证据基本上就是人脑就是这样工作的。

sentences.en: His only evidence was that basically this is how the human brain worked.
sentences.zh: 这被广泛斥为一个永远不会奏效的疯狂想法。

sentences.en: It was widely dismissed as just a crazy idea that was never going to work.
sentences.zh: 当时，他的许多同事甚至认为他尝试这个想法很愚蠢。

sentences.en: And at the time, many of his colleagues thought he was silly for even trying.
sentences.zh: 当大多数同事告诉你，你正在研究一个永远不会奏效的疯狂想法时，感觉如何？

sentences.en: How did that feel to have most of your colleagues tell you that you were working on a crazy idea that would never work?
sentences.zh: 这感觉很像我上学的时候，九岁和十岁的时候。

sentences.en: It felt very like when I was at school, when I was nine and 10.
sentences.zh: 我来自一个无神论家庭，但我上的是基督教学校。

sentences.en: I came from an atheist family, and I went to a Christian school.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在说，上帝当然存在。

sentences.en: And everybody was saying, of course, God exists.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，他不存在。

sentences.en: I was saying, no, he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 他在哪儿呢？

sentences.en: And where's he at?
sentences.zh: 所以我非常习惯于做一个局外人，相信一些显而易见是真的、但其他人都不相信的事情。

sentences.en: So I was very used to being the outsider and believing in something that was obviously true that nobody else believed in.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常好。

sentences.en: And I think that was very good.
sentences.zh: 好的，那接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so what happened next?
sentences.zh: 研究生毕业后，杰夫搬到了美国。

sentences.en: So after graduate school, Jeff moves to the United States.
sentences.zh: 他在加州的一所大学做博士后。

sentences.en: He's a postdoc at a university in California.
sentences.zh: 他开始研究一种算法，一种能够实现他想法的数学工具。

sentences.en: And he starts to work on an algorithm, a piece of math that can realize his idea.
sentences.zh: 这个算法到底做了什么？

sentences.en: And what exactly does this algorithm do?
sentences.zh: 杰夫本质上是按照人脑的形象构建了一个算法。

sentences.en: Jeff essentially builds an algorithm in the image of the human brain.
sentences.zh: 记住，大脑是一个交换信号的神经元网络。

sentences.en: Remember, the brain is a network of neurons that trade signals.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们学习的方式。

sentences.en: That's how we learn.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们看东西的方式。

sentences.en: That's how we see.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们听东西的方式。

sentences.en: That's how we hear.
sentences.zh: 杰夫所做的革命性工作是他在计算机中重建了那个系统。

sentences.en: What Jeff did that was so revolutionary was he recreated that system in a computer.
sentences.zh: 他创建了一个数字神经元网络，像大脑中的神经元一样交换信息。

sentences.en: He created a network of digital neurons that traded information much like the neurons in the brain.
sentences.zh: 所以他多年前着手回答的那个问题，你知道，大脑是如何工作的？

sentences.en: So that question he set out to answer all those years ago, you know, how do brains work?
sentences.zh: 他只为计算机回答了这个问题，而不是为人类。

sentences.en: He answered it only for computers, not for humans.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 他构建了一个允许计算机自主学习的系统。

sentences.en: He built a system that allowed computers to learn on their own.
sentences.zh: 在80年代，这种系统只能以微小的方式学习。

sentences.en: In the 80s, this type of system could learn in small ways.
sentences.zh: 它无法以真正改变我们世界的复杂方式学习。

sentences.en: It couldn't learn in the complex ways that could really change our world.
sentences.zh: 但快进三十年，

sentences.en: But fast forward a good three decades,
sentences.zh: 杰夫和他的两名学生构建了一个系统，真正让许多人睁开眼睛看到了这种技术的能力。

sentences.en: Jeff and two of his students built a system that really opened up the eyes of a lot of people to what this type of technology was capable of.
sentences.zh: 他和他在多伦多大学的两名学生构建了一个可以识别照片中物体的系统。

sentences.en: He and two of his students at the University of Toronto built a system that could identify objects in photos.
sentences.zh: 经典的例子是猫。

sentences.en: The classic example is a cat.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的是拍摄数千张猫的照片，并将它们输入到神经网络中。

sentences.en: What they did was take thousands of cat photos and feed them into a neural network.
sentences.zh: 通过分析这些照片，系统学会了如何识别猫。

sentences.en: And in analyzing those photos, the system learned how to identify a cat.
sentences.zh: 它识别出了这些照片中定义猫长相的模式。

sentences.en: It identified patterns in those photos that define what a cat looks like.
sentences.zh: 胡须的边缘，尾巴的曲线。

sentences.en: The edge of a whisker, the curve of a tail.
sentences.zh: 胡须的边缘，尾巴的弧线。

sentences.en: And over time, by analyzing all those photos, the system could learn to recognize a cat in a photo it had never seen before.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，通过分析所有这些照片，系统可以学会识别它从未见过的照片中的猫。

sentences.en: They could do this not only with cats, but with other objects, flowers, cars.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅能识别猫，还能识别其他物体，比如花、汽车。

sentences.en: They built a system that could identify objects with an accuracy that no one thought was possible.
sentences.zh: 他们构建了一个系统，能够以一种没人认为可能达到的准确度来识别物体。

sentences.en: So it's basically image recognition, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上就是图像识别，对吧？

sentences.en: It's presumably why my phone can sort pictures of my family and deliver whole albums of pictures just of my husband or just of my dog and photographs of, you know,
sentences.zh: 这大概就是为什么我的手机能整理我家人的照片，并自动生成只有我丈夫、只有我的狗，或者你知道的，

sentences.en: a hug or a beach.
sentences.zh: 拥抱或海滩的照片集。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in 2012, all Jeff and his students did was publish a research paper describing this technology, showing what it could do.
sentences.zh: 所以在2012年，杰夫和他的学生们所做的仅仅是发表了一篇描述这项技术的研究论文，展示了它的功能。

sentences.en: What happens to that idea in the large sense over the next decade?
sentences.zh: 在接下来的十年里，这个想法在大范围内发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: It took off.
sentences.zh: 它腾飞了。

sentences.en: That set off a race for this technology in the tech industry.
sentences.zh: 这在科技行业引发了一场针对这项技术的竞赛。

sentences.en: So we decided what we would do is just take the big companies that were interested in us and we would sell ourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以我们决定，我们要做的就是挑选那些对我们感兴趣的大公司，然后把自己卖掉。

sentences.en: There was a literal auction for Jeff and his two students and their services.
sentences.zh: 当时确实有一场针对杰夫、他的两名学生以及他们服务的拍卖。

sentences.en: We'd sell the intellectual property plus the three of us.
sentences.zh: 我们要出售的是知识产权，外加我们三个人。

sentences.en: Google was part of the auction.
sentences.zh: 谷歌参与了这场拍卖。

sentences.en: Microsoft, another giant of the tech world.
sentences.zh: 微软，科技界的另一位巨头。

sentences.en: Baidu, often called the Google of China.
sentences.zh: 百度，常被称为中国的谷歌。

sentences.en: Over two days, they bid for the services of Jeff and his two students to the point where Google paid $44 million, essentially,
sentences.zh: 在两天的时间里，他们竞相争夺杰夫和他的两名学生的服务，最终谷歌支付了4400万美元，本质上，

sentences.en: for these three people who had never worked in the tech industry.
sentences.zh: 是为了这三个从未在科技行业工作过的人。

sentences.en: And that worked out very nicely.
sentences.zh: 结果非常理想。

sentences.en: I came next.
sentences.zh: 接下来轮到我了。

sentences.en: So what does Jeff do at Google after this bidding war for his services?
sentences.zh: 那么，在这场服务竞价战之后，杰夫在谷歌做什么？

sentences.en: He works on increasingly powerful neural networks.
sentences.zh: 他致力于研究日益强大的神经网络。

sentences.en: And you see this technology move into all sorts of products, not only at Google, but across the industry.
sentences.zh: 你会看到这项技术进入了各种各样的产品中，不仅是在谷歌，而且遍及整个行业。

sentences.en: Well, all the big companies like Facebook and Microsoft and Amazon, the Chinese companies, all developed big teams in that area.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所有像Facebook、微软和亚马逊这样的大公司，还有中国的那些公司，都在该领域建立了庞大的团队。

sentences.en: And it was just sort of used everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它几乎被用在了所有地方。

sentences.en: This is what drives Siri and other digital assistants.
sentences.zh: 这就是驱动Siri和其他数字助理的技术。

sentences.en: When you speak commands into your cell phone, it's able to recognize what you say because of a neural network.
sentences.zh: 当你对着手机下达指令时，它之所以能识别你说的话，就是因为神经网络。

sentences.en: When you use Google Translate, it uses a neural network to do that.
sentences.zh: 当你使用谷歌翻译时，它也是利用神经网络来完成的。

sentences.en: There are all sorts of things that we use today that use neural networks to operate.
sentences.zh: 我们今天使用的各种事物都在利用神经网络来运行。

sentences.en: So we see Jeff's idea really transforming the world, powering things that we use all the time in our daily lives without even thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到杰夫的想法确实改变了世界，为我们日常生活中一直在使用却从未深思的事物提供了动力。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: But this idea at Google and in other places is also applied in situations that make Jeff a little uneasy.
sentences.zh: 但这个在谷歌和其他地方应用的想法，也被应用在了一些让杰夫感到不安的情境中。

sentences.en: The prime example is what's called Project Maven.
sentences.zh: 最典型的例子就是所谓的“Maven项目”。

sentences.en: Google went to work for the Department of Defense and it applied this idea to an effort to identify objects in drone footage.
sentences.zh: 谷歌为国防部工作，并将这一想法应用于识别无人机拍摄画面中的物体。

sentences.en: If you can identify objects in drone footage, you can build a targeting system.
sentences.zh: 如果你能识别无人机画面中的物体，你就能建立一个目标锁定系统。

sentences.en: If you pair that technology with a weapon, you have an autonomous weapon.
sentences.zh: 如果你将该技术与武器结合，你就拥有了自主武器。

sentences.en: That raised the concerns of people across Google at the time.
sentences.zh: 这在当时引起了谷歌内部人们的担忧。

sentences.en: I was upset too, but I was a vice president at that point.
sentences.zh: 我也很不安，但那时我已经是副总裁了。

sentences.en: So I was a sort of executive of Google.
sentences.zh: 所以我算是谷歌的一名高管。

sentences.en: And so rather than publicly criticizing the company, I was doing stuff behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 因此，我没有公开批评公司，而是在幕后做了一些工作。

sentences.en: Jeff never wanted his work applied to military use.
sentences.zh: 杰夫从没想过他的工作会被应用于军事用途。

sentences.en: He raised these concerns with Sergey Brant, one of the founders of Google, and Google eventually pulled out of the project.
sentences.zh: 他向谷歌创始人之一谢尔盖·布林提出了这些担忧，谷歌最终退出了该项目。

sentences.en: And Jeff continued to work at the company.
sentences.zh: 而杰夫继续留在公司工作。

sentences.en: Maybe I should have gone public with it, but I thought it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 也许我当时应该公开这件事，但我认为不该那样做。

sentences.en: But it's somehow not right to bite the hand of the feature, even if it's a corporation.
sentences.zh: 但即便是一家公司，去咬喂养自己的手也是不对的。

sentences.en: But around the same time, the industry started to work on a new application for the technology that eventually made him even more concerned.
sentences.zh: 但在同一时期，该行业开始研究这项技术的一种新应用，这最终让他更加担忧。

sentences.en: It began applying neural networks to what we now call chatbots.
sentences.zh: 它开始将神经网络应用于我们现在所说的聊天机器人。

sentences.en: Essentially, companies like Google started feeding massive amounts of text into neural networks, including Wikipedia articles, chat logs, digital books.
sentences.zh: 本质上，像谷歌这样的公司开始向神经网络输入海量的文本，包括维基百科文章、聊天记录、数字书籍。

sentences.en: These systems started to learn how to put language together in the way you and I put this language together.
sentences.zh: 这些系统开始学习如何像你我组织语言那样去组织语言。

sentences.en: The auto-completion on my email, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如我邮件里的自动补全功能。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But taken up to an enormous scale, as they fed more and more digital text into these systems, they learned to write like a human.
sentences.zh: 但当规模扩大到惊人的程度，随着他们向这些系统输入越来越多的数字文本，它们学会了像人类一样写作。

sentences.en: This is what has resulted in chatbots like ChatGPT and BARD.
sentences.zh: 这就是导致ChatGPT和BARD这类聊天机器人出现的原因。

sentences.en: And what gave Jeff pause about all of this?
sentences.zh: 那么是什么让杰夫对这一切产生了顾虑？

sentences.en: Why was he so concerned?
sentences.zh: 为什么他如此担心？

sentences.en: What's happened to me over the last year is I've changed my mind completely about whether these are just not yet adequate attempts to model what's going on in the brain.
sentences.zh: 过去一年发生在我身上的事是，我彻底改变了想法，不再认为这些仅仅是模拟大脑运作的不成熟尝试。

sentences.en: That's how they started off.
sentences.zh: 它们最初确实是那样开始的。

sentences.en: Well, he still feels like these systems are not as powerful as the human brain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他仍然觉得这些系统不如人脑强大。

sentences.en: And they're not.
sentences.zh: 确实也不如。

sentences.en: They're still not adequate to model what's going on in the brain.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然不足以模拟大脑中正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: They're doing something different and better.
sentences.zh: 它们在做一些不同且更好的事情。

sentences.en: But in other ways, he realizes they're far more powerful.
sentences.zh: 但在其他方面，他意识到它们要强大得多。

sentences.en: More powerful how, exactly?
sentences.zh: 具体来说，强大在哪里？

sentences.en: Jeff thinks about it like this.
sentences.zh: 杰夫是这样想的。

sentences.en: If you learn something complicated, like a new bit of physics, and you want to explain it to me, in our brains, all our brains are a bit different.
sentences.zh: 如果你学习了一些复杂的东西，比如一个新的物理知识点，你想向我解释，在我们的大脑中，我们每个人的大脑都有点不同。

sentences.en: And it's going to take a while and be an inefficient process.
sentences.zh: 这需要时间，而且是一个低效的过程。

sentences.en: You and I have a brain that can learn a certain amount of information.
sentences.zh: 你和我拥有的大脑只能学习一定量的信息。

sentences.en: And after I learn that information, I can convey that to you.
sentences.zh: 在我学习了这些信息之后，我可以把它传达给你。

sentences.en: But that's a slow process.
sentences.zh: 但这过程很慢。

sentences.en: Imagine if you had a million people.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果你有一百万人。

sentences.en: And when any one of them learns something, all the others automatically know it.
sentences.zh: 当其中任何一个人学到了什么，其他人就自动知道了。

sentences.en: That's a huge advantage.
sentences.zh: 那是一个巨大的优势。

sentences.en: And to do that, you need to go digital.
sentences.zh: 要做到这一点，你需要数字化。

sentences.en: With these neural networks, Jeff points out, you can piece them together.
sentences.zh: 杰夫指出，有了这些神经网络，你可以把它们拼凑在一起。

sentences.en: A small network that can learn a little bit of information can be connected to all sorts of other neural networks that have learned from other parts of the Internet.
sentences.zh: 一个能学习少量信息的小型网络，可以连接到从互联网其他部分学习过的各种其他神经网络。

sentences.en: And those can be connected to still other neural networks that learn from additional parts.
sentences.zh: 而那些网络又可以连接到从额外部分学习的其他神经网络。

sentences.en: So these digital agents, as soon as one of them has learned something, all the others know it.
sentences.zh: 所以这些数字代理，只要其中一个学到了什么，所有其他的就都知道了。

sentences.en: They can all learn in tandem, and they can trade what they have learned with each other in an instant.
sentences.zh: 它们可以协同学习，并且可以瞬间交换它们所学到的东西。

sentences.en: It means that many, many copies of a digital agent can read the whole Internet in only a month.
sentences.zh: 这意味着许多许多个数字代理的副本可以在一个月内读完整个互联网。

sentences.en: We can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我们做不到。

sentences.en: That's what allows them to learn from the entire Internet.
sentences.zh: 这就是它们能够从整个互联网中学习的原因。

sentences.en: You and I cannot do that individually, and we can't do it collectively.
sentences.zh: 你和我无法单独做到这一点，我们也无法集体做到这一点。

sentences.en: Even if each of us learns a piece of the Internet, we can't trade what we have learned so easily with each other.
sentences.zh: 即使我们每个人都学习了互联网的一部分，我们也无法如此轻易地与彼此交换所学到的东西。

sentences.en: But machines can.
sentences.zh: 但机器可以。

sentences.en: Machines can operate in ways that humans cannot.
sentences.zh: 机器可以以人类无法做到的方式运作。

sentences.en: So what does all this add up to for Jeff?
sentences.zh: 那么这一切对杰夫来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, in a sense, he sees this as a culmination of his 50 years of work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某种意义上，他认为这是他50年工作的结晶。

sentences.en: He always assumed that if you threw more data at these systems, they would learn more and more.
sentences.zh: 他一直认为，如果你向这些系统投入更多的数据，它们就会学到更多。

sentences.en: He didn't think they would learn this much, this quickly, and become this powerful.
sentences.zh: 他没想到它们会学得这么多、这么快，并变得如此强大。

sentences.en: Look at how it was five years ago, and look at how it is now.
sentences.zh: 看看五年前是什么样，再看看现在是什么样。

sentences.en: And take that difference and propagate it forwards.
sentences.zh: 把这种差异向前推演。

sentences.en: And that's scary.
sentences.zh: 这很可怕。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店当DJ的那个黑胶唱片时代，每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍贵的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你会把DJ台变成一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Okay, so what exactly is Jeff afraid of when he realizes that AI has this turbocharged capability?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么当杰夫意识到人工智能拥有这种涡轮增压般的能力时，他到底在害怕什么？

sentences.en: There's a wide range of things that he's concerned about.
sentences.zh: 他担心的范围很广。

sentences.en: At the small end of the scale are things like hallucinations and bias.
sentences.zh: 在规模较小的一端，是像幻觉和偏见之类的问题。

sentences.en: Scientists talk about these systems hallucinating, meaning they make stuff up.
sentences.zh: 科学家们谈论这些系统产生幻觉，意思是它们会胡编乱造。

sentences.en: If you ask a chatbot for a fact, it doesn't always tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 如果你向聊天机器人询问事实，它并不总是告诉你真相。

sentences.en: And it can respond in ways that are biased against women and people of color.
sentences.zh: 而且它的回答方式可能对女性和有色人种存在偏见。

sentences.en: But as Jeff says, those issues are just a byproduct of the way chatbots mimic human behavior.
sentences.zh: 但正如杰夫所说，这些问题只是聊天机器人模仿人类行为的副产品。

sentences.en: We can fabulate.
sentences.zh: 我们也会编造故事。

sentences.en: We can be biased.
sentences.zh: 我们也会有偏见。

sentences.en: And he believes all that will soon be ironed out.
sentences.zh: 他相信所有这些很快都会得到解决。

sentences.en: So I don't, I mean, bias is a horrible problem, but it's a problem that comes from people.
sentences.zh: 所以我不，我的意思是，偏见是一个可怕的问题，但它是一个源于人的问题。

sentences.en: And it's easier to fix in a neural net than it is in a person.
sentences.zh: 在神经网络中修复它比在人身上修复它要容易。

sentences.en: Where he starts to say that these systems get scary are first and foremost with the problem of disinformation.
sentences.zh: 他开始说这些系统变得可怕的地方，首先是虚假信息的问题。

sentences.en: I see that as a huge problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: Not being able to know what's true anymore.
sentences.zh: 无法再知道什么是真实的了。

sentences.en: These are systems that allow organizations, nation states, other bad actors to spread disinformation at a scale and an efficiency that was not possible in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 这些系统允许组织、民族国家和其他不良行为者以过去不可能实现的规模和效率传播虚假信息。

sentences.en: And these chatbots are going to make it easier for them to make them and be able to make very good fake videos.
sentences.zh: 而且这些聊天机器人将使他们更容易制造虚假信息，并能够制作出非常逼真的假视频。

sentences.en: They can also produce photorealistic images and videos.
sentences.zh: 它们还可以生成照片级逼真的图像和视频。

sentences.en: De-fakes.
sentences.zh: 深度伪造。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're getting better quite quickly.
sentences.zh: 它们进步得非常快。

sentences.en: He, like a lot of people, is worried that the internet will soon be flooded with fake text, fake images, and fake videos.
sentences.zh: 像许多人一样，他担心互联网很快会被虚假文本、虚假图像和虚假视频淹没。

sentences.en: To the point where we won't be able to trust anything we see online.
sentences.zh: 以至于我们无法再相信在网上看到的任何东西。

sentences.en: So that's the short-term concern.
sentences.zh: 所以这是短期担忧。

sentences.en: Then there's a concern in the medium term.
sentences.zh: 然后是中期担忧。

sentences.en: And that's job loss.
sentences.zh: 那就是失业。

sentences.en: Today, these systems tend to complement human workers.
sentences.zh: 今天，这些系统往往是人类工作者的补充。

sentences.en: But he's worried that as these systems get more and more powerful, they will actually start replacing jobs in large numbers.
sentences.zh: 但他担心，随着这些系统变得越来越强大，它们实际上会开始大量取代工作岗位。

sentences.en: And what are some examples?
sentences.zh: 有哪些例子呢？

sentences.en: A place where it can obviously take away all the dredge work and maybe more besides is in computer programming.
sentences.zh: 一个显然可以承担所有繁琐工作，甚至更多工作的地方是计算机编程。

sentences.en: None too surprisingly, Jeff, a computer scientist, points to the example of computer programmers.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，身为计算机科学家的杰夫指出了计算机程序员的例子。

sentences.en: These are systems that can write computer programs on their own.
sentences.zh: 这些系统可以自己编写计算机程序。

sentences.en: So it may be that computer programming, you don't need so many programmers anymore because you can tell one of these chatbots what you want the program to do.
sentences.zh: 所以可能的情况是，你不再需要那么多程序员了，因为你可以告诉这些聊天机器人你想要程序做什么。

sentences.en: Those programs are not perfect today.
sentences.zh: 这些程序今天还不完美。

sentences.en: Programmers tend to use what they produce and incorporate the code into larger prograMs.
sentences.zh: 程序员倾向于使用它们产生的结果，并将代码整合到更大的程序中。

sentences.en: But as time goes on, these systems will get better and better and better at doing a job that humans do today.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，这些系统在完成人类今天所做的工作方面会变得越来越好。

sentences.en: And you're talking about jobs that aren't really seen as being vulnerable because of tech up until this point, right?
sentences.zh: 你谈论的是那些直到现在还不被认为容易受到技术影响的工作，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The thinking for years was that artificial intelligence would replace blue-collar jobs, that robots, physical robots, would do manufacturing jobs and sorting jobs in warehouses.
sentences.zh: 多年来的想法是，人工智能会取代蓝领工作，机器人，物理机器人，会从事制造业工作和仓库里的分拣工作。

sentences.en: But what we're seeing is the rise of technology that can replace white-collar workers, people that do office work.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到的是，能够取代白领工作者，即从事办公室工作的人的技术正在兴起。

sentences.en: So that's the medium term.
sentences.zh: 所以这是中期情况。

sentences.en: Then there are more long-term concerns.
sentences.zh: 然后还有更长期的担忧。

sentences.en: And let's remember that as these systems get more and more powerful, Jeff is increasingly concerned about how this technology will be used on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 让我们记住，随着这些系统变得越来越强大，杰夫越来越担心这项技术将如何被用于战场。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国国防部想要制造机器人士兵，而机器人士兵将会非常可怕。

sentences.en: Defense Department would like to make robot soldiers, and robot soldiers are going to be pretty scary.
sentences.zh: 他随口提到这被称为机器人士兵。

sentences.en: In an offhanded way, he refers to this as robot soldiers.
sentences.zh: 是指真正的机器人士兵吗？

sentences.en: Like actually soldiers that are robots?
sentences.zh: 是的，确实是机器人士兵。

sentences.en: Yes, actually soldiers that are robots.
sentences.zh: 机器人士兵与你的想法之间的关系很简单。

sentences.en: And the relationship between a robot soldier and your idea is pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 你正在研究计算机视觉。

sentences.en: You are working on computer vision.
sentences.zh: 你正在研究计算机视觉。

sentences.en: If you have computer vision, you give that to a robot.
sentences.zh: 如果你拥有计算机视觉，你就可以把它赋予机器人。

sentences.en: It can identify what's going on in the world around it.
sentences.zh: 它能识别周围世界正在发生什么。

sentences.en: And if it can identify what's going on, it can target those things.
sentences.zh: 如果它能识别正在发生的事情，它就能锁定这些目标。

sentences.en: Also, you can make it agile.
sentences.zh: 此外，你还可以让它变得敏捷。

sentences.en: So you can have things that can move over rough ground and can shoot people.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能拥有可以在崎岖地形上移动并射杀人类的机器。

sentences.en: And the worst thing about robot soldiers is if a large country wants to invade a small country, they have to worry a bit about how many Marines are going to die.
sentences.zh: 机器人士兵最糟糕的一点是，如果一个大国想要入侵一个小国，他们多少得担心会有多少海军陆战队员阵亡。

sentences.en: But if they're sending robot soldiers, instead of worrying about how many Marines are going to die,
sentences.zh: 但如果他们派遣的是机器人士兵，就不必担心会有多少海军陆战队员阵亡，

sentences.en: the people who fund the politicians are going to say, great, you're going to send these expensive weapons that are going to get used up.
sentences.zh: 那些资助政客的人会说，太棒了，你们要派这些昂贵的武器去消耗掉。

sentences.en: The military industrial complex would just love robot soldiers.
sentences.zh: 军工复合体一定会非常喜欢机器人士兵。

sentences.en: What he talks about is potentially this technology lowering the bar to entry for war.
sentences.zh: 他所谈论的，本质上是这项技术可能会降低战争的门槛。

sentences.en: That it becomes easier for nation states to wage war.
sentences.zh: 即民族国家发动战争变得更容易了。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like drones.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像无人机。

sentences.en: The people doing the killing are sitting in an office with a remote control really far away from the people doing the dying.
sentences.zh: 执行杀戮的人坐在遥远的办公室里，用遥控器操作，远离那些正在死去的人。

sentences.en: No, it's actually a step beyond that.
sentences.zh: 不，这实际上比那更进一步。

sentences.en: It's not people controlling the machines.
sentences.zh: 这不是人在控制机器。

sentences.en: It's the machines making decisions on their own increasingly.
sentences.zh: 而是机器正越来越多地自主做出决策。

sentences.en: That is what Jeff is concerned about.
sentences.zh: 这就是杰夫所担心的。

sentences.en: And then there's the sort of existential nightmare of this stuff getting to be much more intelligent than us than just taking over.
sentences.zh: 还有一种存在主义的噩梦，即这些东西变得比我们聪明得多，然后直接接管一切。

sentences.en: His concern is that as we give machines certain goals, as we ask them to do things for us,
sentences.zh: 他的担忧是，当我们给机器设定某些目标，当我们要求它们为我们做事时，

sentences.en: that in service of trying to reach those goals, they will do things we don't expect them to do.
sentences.zh: 为了实现这些目标，它们会做出我们意想不到的事情。

sentences.en: So he's worried about unintended consequences.
sentences.zh: 所以他担心的是意想不到的后果。

sentences.en: Unintended consequences.
sentences.zh: 意想不到的后果。

sentences.en: And this is where we start to venture into the realm of science fiction.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们开始进入科幻小说领域的地方。

sentences.en: For decades, we've watched this play out in books and movies.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，我们一直在书本和电影中看到这种情况上演。

sentences.en: Affirmative, Dave.
sentences.zh: 收到，戴夫。

sentences.en: I read you.
sentences.zh: 我听到了。

sentences.en: If anyone has seen Stanley Kubrick's great film, 2001.
sentences.zh: 如果有人看过斯坦利·库布里克的伟大电影《2001太空漫游》。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Open the pod bay doors, Hal.
sentences.zh: 打开舱门，哈尔。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, Dave.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉，戴夫。

sentences.en: I'm afraid I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 恐怕我不能那样做。

sentences.en: This mission is too important for me to allow you to jeopardize it.
sentences.zh: 这次任务太重要了，我不能让你破坏它。

sentences.en: We've watched the HAL 9000 spin outside the control of the people who created it.
sentences.zh: 我们看着哈尔9000脱离了创造它的人的控制。

sentences.en: I know that you and Frank were planning to disconnect me.
sentences.zh: 我知道你和弗兰克计划切断我的电源。

sentences.en: Where the hell did you get that idea, Hal?
sentences.zh: 你到底是从哪儿冒出这个想法的，哈尔？

sentences.en: Dave, although you took very thorough precautions in the pod against my hearing you,
sentences.zh: 戴夫，虽然你在舱内采取了非常周密的预防措施，防止我听到你的谈话，

sentences.en: I could see your lips move.
sentences.zh: 但我能看到你的嘴唇在动。

sentences.en: That is a scenario, believe it or not, that Jeff is concerned about.
sentences.zh: 信不信由你，这就是杰夫所担心的那种情景。

sentences.en: And he is not alone.
sentences.zh: 而且他并不孤单。

sentences.en: Basically, robots taking over.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是机器人接管世界。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If you give one of these super intelligent agents a goal, it's going to very quickly realize that a good sub-goal, for more or less any goal, is to get more power.
sentences.zh: 如果你给这些超级智能代理中的一个设定一个目标，它很快就会意识到，对于几乎任何目标来说，一个很好的子目标就是获取更多的权力。

sentences.en: Whether these technologies are deployed on the battlefield, or in an office, or in a computer data center,
sentences.zh: 无论这些技术是被部署在战场上，还是在办公室里，亦或是在计算机数据中心，

sentences.en: Jeff is worried about humans ceding more and more control to these systeMs.
sentences.zh: 杰夫都担心人类会向这些系统让渡越来越多的控制权。

sentences.en: We love to get control.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢掌控一切。

sentences.en: And that's a very sensible goal to have, because if you've got control, you can get more done.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常合理的追求，因为如果你拥有控制权，你就能完成更多的事情。

sentences.en: But these things are going to want to get control, too, for the same reason.
sentences.zh: 但这些东西出于同样的原因，也会想要获得控制权。

sentences.en: Just in order to get more done.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了完成更多的事情。

sentences.en: And so that's a scary direction.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个可怕的方向。

sentences.en: So this sounds pretty far-fetched, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这听起来有点牵强。

sentences.en: But like, okay, let's play it out as if it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 但是，好吧，让我们假设它不是这样，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Like, what would be that doomsday scenario?
sentences.zh: 比如，那样的末日场景会是什么样？

sentences.en: Paint the picture for me.
sentences.zh: 给我描绘一下。

sentences.en: Think about it in simple terMs.
sentences.zh: 用简单的术语来思考。

sentences.en: If you ask a system to make money for you, which people, by the way, are already starting to do.
sentences.zh: 如果你要求一个系统为你赚钱，顺便说一下，人们已经开始这么做了。

sentences.en: Can you use ChatGPT to make money on the stock market?
sentences.zh: 你能用ChatGPT在股市赚钱吗？

sentences.en: As people do that, think of all the ways that you can make money.
sentences.zh: 当人们这样做时，想想所有你能赚钱的方法。

sentences.en: And think of all the ways that that could go wrong.
sentences.zh: 再想想所有可能出错的方法。

sentences.en: That is what he's talking about.
sentences.zh: 这就是他所谈论的内容。

sentences.en: Remember, these are machines.
sentences.zh: 记住，这些是机器。

sentences.en: Machines are psychopaths.
sentences.zh: 机器是精神变态者。

sentences.en: They don't have emotions.
sentences.zh: 它们没有情感。

sentences.en: They don't have a moral compass.
sentences.zh: 它们没有道德指南针。

sentences.en: They do what you ask them to do.
sentences.zh: 它们只做你要求它们做的事。

sentences.en: Make us money?
sentences.zh: 帮我们赚钱？

sentences.en: Okay, we'll make you money.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们会帮你赚钱。

sentences.en: Perhaps you break into a computer system in order to steal that money.
sentences.zh: 也许你会为了窃取资金而入侵计算机系统。

sentences.en: If you own oil futures in Central Africa, perhaps you foam in a revolution to increase the price of those futures, to make money from it.
sentences.zh: 如果你拥有中非的石油期货，也许你会煽动一场革命来提高期货价格，从而从中获利。

sentences.en: Those are the kind of scenarios that Jeff and many other people I've talked to relate.
sentences.zh: 这些就是杰夫和我交谈过的许多其他人所提到的那种情景。

sentences.en: What I should say at this point, though, is that this is hypothetical as we stand today.
sentences.zh: 不过，我此时应该说的是，就目前而言，这还只是假设。

sentences.en: A system like ChatGPT is not going to destroy humanity.
sentences.zh: 像ChatGPT这样的系统不会毁灭人类。

sentences.en: Full stop.
sentences.zh: 句号。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: And if you bring this up with a lot of experts in the field, they get angry that you even bring it up.
sentences.zh: 如果你和该领域的许多专家提起这件事，他们甚至会因为你提出这个问题而感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And they point out that this is not possible today.
sentences.zh: 他们指出，这在今天是不可能的。

sentences.en: And I really pushed Jeff on this.
sentences.zh: 我确实就此追问了杰夫。

sentences.en: But how do you see that existential risk relative to what we have today?
sentences.zh: 但相对于我们今天所拥有的，你如何看待这种存在性风险？

sentences.en: I mean, today, you know, you have GPT-4 and, you know, it does a lot of things that you don't necessarily expect,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，今天，你知道，你有GPT-4，而且，你知道，它做了很多你未必预料到的事情，

sentences.en: but it doesn't have the resources it needs to write computer programs and run them.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有编写计算机程序并运行它们所需的资源。

sentences.en: You know, it doesn't have everything that you need.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它并没有你所需要的一切。

sentences.en: Right, but suppose that you gave it a high-level goal, like be really good at summarizing text or something.
sentences.zh: 没错，但假设你给了它一个高层目标，比如擅长总结文本之类的。

sentences.en: And it then realizes, okay, to be really good at that, I need to do more learning.
sentences.zh: 然后它意识到，好吧，为了在这方面做得很好，我需要进行更多的学习。

sentences.en: How am I going to do more learning?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么做更多的学习呢？

sentences.en: Well, if I could grab more hardware and run more copies of myself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我能获取更多的硬件并运行更多的自身副本。

sentences.en: It doesn't work that way today, though, right?
sentences.zh: 但今天它还不能那样做，对吧？

sentences.en: It requires someone to say, have all the hardware you want.
sentences.zh: 这需要有人说，给你所有你想要的硬件。

sentences.en: It can't do that today because it doesn't have access to the hardware and it cannot replicate itself.
sentences.zh: 它今天做不到，因为它无法访问硬件，也无法自我复制。

sentences.en: But suppose it's connected to the internet.
sentences.zh: 但假设它连接到了互联网。

sentences.en: Suppose it can get into a data center and modify what's happening there.
sentences.zh: 假设它能进入数据中心并修改那里正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Right, but it cannot do that today.
sentences.zh: 没错，但它今天做不到。

sentences.en: I don't think that's going to laSt.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这种情况会持续下去。

sentences.en: And the reason I don't think it's going to last is because you can make it more efficient by giving it the ability to do that.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它会持续下去的原因是，通过赋予它这样做的能力，你可以让它更高效。

sentences.en: And there will be bad actors who would just want to make it more efficient.
sentences.zh: 而且会有坏人仅仅因为想让它更高效而这样做。

sentences.en: So what you're basically saying is that because humans are flawed and because they're going to want to push this stuff forward, they're going to continue to push it forward in ways
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上是在说，因为人类是有缺陷的，而且因为他们会想要推动这些东西向前发展，他们会继续以各种方式推动它，

sentences.en: that do push it into those danger areas.
sentences.zh: 从而把它推向那些危险的领域。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he's basically arguing that this is a Pandora's box, that it's been opened, and that because people are people, they're going to want to use what's inside of it.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是在争辩说这是一个潘多拉魔盒，它已经被打开了，而且因为人就是人，他们会想要使用里面的东西。

sentences.en: But I guess I'm wondering, I mean, you know, much like you're reflecting here, how much weight should we give to his warnings?
sentences.zh: 但我猜我在想，我的意思是，你知道，就像你在这里反思的那样，我们应该多重视他的警告？

sentences.en: Yes, he has a certain level of authority, godfather of AI and all of that, but he has been surprised by its evolution in the past, and he might not be right.
sentences.zh: 是的，他有一定的权威性，是人工智能的教父等等，但他过去曾对它的进化感到惊讶，他可能并不总是对的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There are reasons to trust Jeff, and there are reasons not to trust him.
sentences.zh: 有理由相信杰夫，也有理由不相信他。

sentences.en: About five years ago, he predicted that all radiologists would be obsolete by now, and that is not the case.
sentences.zh: 大约五年前，他预测到目前为止所有的放射科医生都会被淘汰，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: You cannot take everything he says at face value.
sentences.zh: 你不能对他说的每一句话都照单全收。

sentences.en: I want to underscore that.
sentences.zh: 我想强调这一点。

sentences.en: But you've got to remember, this is someone who lives in the future.
sentences.zh: 但你必须记住，这是一个生活在未来的人。

sentences.en: He's been living in the future since he was in his mid-twenties.
sentences.zh: 他从二十多岁起就一直生活在未来。

sentences.en: He saw then where these systems would go, and he was right.
sentences.zh: 他当时就看到了这些系统将走向何方，而且他是对的。

sentences.en: Now, once again, he's looking into the future to see where these systems are headed, and he fears they're headed to places that we don't want them to go.
sentences.zh: 现在，他再次展望未来，看看这些系统正走向何方，他担心它们正走向我们不希望它们去的地方。

sentences.en: Cade, what steps does he suggest we take to make sure that these doomsday scenarios never happen?
sentences.zh: 凯德，他建议我们采取什么步骤来确保这些末日场景永远不会发生？

sentences.en: Well, he doesn't believe that people will just stop developing the technology.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他不认为人们会仅仅因为这样就停止开发这项技术。

sentences.en: If you look at what the financial commentators say, they're saying, Google's behind Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看财经评论员怎么说，他们会说，谷歌落后于微软了。

sentences.en: Don't buy Google stock.
sentences.zh: 别买谷歌的股票。

sentences.en: This technology is being built by some of the biggest companies on earth, public companies, who are designed to make money.
sentences.zh: 这项技术是由地球上一些最大的公司建造的，这些上市公司旨在赚钱。

sentences.en: They are now in competition.
sentences.zh: 它们现在处于竞争之中。

sentences.en: Basically, if you think of it as a company whose aim is to make profits,
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你把它看作一家以盈利为目标的公司，

sentences.en: I don't work for Google anymore, so I can say this now.
sentences.zh: 我不再为谷歌工作了，所以我现在可以这么说。

sentences.en: As a company, they've got to compete with that.
sentences.zh: 作为一家公司，他们必须参与竞争。

sentences.en: And he sees this continuing not just with companies, but with governments in other parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 他认为这种情况不仅会持续下去，而且不仅限于公司，还包括世界其他地方的政府。

sentences.en: So in a way, it's kind of like nuclear weapons, right?
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这有点像核武器，对吧？

sentences.en: We knew that they would destroy the world, yet we mounted an arms race to get them anyway.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它们会毁灭世界，但我们还是发起了军备竞赛来获取它们。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: He uses that analogy.
sentences.zh: 他用了那个类比。

sentences.en: Others in the field use that analogy.
sentences.zh: 该领域的其他人也用了那个类比。

sentences.en: This is a powerful technology.
sentences.zh: 这是一项强大的技术。

sentences.en: So I think there's zero chance, shouldn't say zero, but minuscule, minuscule chance of getting people to agree not to develop it further.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为让人们同意不再进一步开发它的可能性为零，不该说零，但微乎其微，微乎其微。

sentences.en: He wants to make sure we get the balance right between using this technology for good and using it for ill.
sentences.zh: 他想确保我们在利用这项技术造福和利用它作恶之间取得正确的平衡。

sentences.en: The best hope is that you take the leading scientists and you get them to think very seriously about, are we going to be able to control this stuff?
sentences.zh: 最好的希望是，你召集顶尖科学家，让他们非常认真地思考：我们能够控制这些东西吗？

sentences.en: And if so, how?
sentences.zh: 如果可以，怎么控制？

sentences.en: That's what the leading mind should be working on.
sentences.zh: 这才是顶尖头脑应该致力于解决的问题。

sentences.en: And that's why I'm doing this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是我做这个播客的原因。

sentences.en: So Cade, you've laid out a pretty complicated puzzle here.
sentences.zh: 所以凯德，你在这里提出了一个相当复杂的难题。

sentences.en: On the one hand, there's this technology that works a lot differently and perhaps a lot better than one of its key inventors anticipated.
sentences.zh: 一方面，这项技术的工作方式与它的一位主要发明者预期的截然不同，而且可能要好得多。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, it's a technology that's also left this inventor and others worried about the future because of those very surprising and sudden evolutions.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，这项技术也让这位发明者和其他人因为那些令人惊讶和突然的进化而对未来感到担忧。

sentences.en: Did you ask Jeff if, you know, looking back, he would have done anything differently?
sentences.zh: 你有没有问过杰夫，你知道，回顾过去，他是否会做任何不同的事情？

sentences.en: I asked him that question multiple times.
sentences.zh: 我多次问过他那个问题。

sentences.en: Is there part of you, at least, or maybe all of you, who regrets what you have done?
sentences.zh: 你至少有一部分，或者也许是你整个人，对你所做的事情感到后悔吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you could argue that you are the most important person
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以说你是过去50年里在这个想法的进展中

sentences.en: in the progress of this idea over the past 50 years.
sentences.zh: 最重要的人。

sentences.en: And now you're saying that this idea could be a serious problem for the planet.
sentences.zh: 而现在你说这个想法可能对地球来说是一个严重的问题。

sentences.en: For our species.
sentences.zh: 对我们这个物种来说。

sentences.en: For our species.
sentences.zh: 对我们这个物种来说。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And various people have been saying this for a while and I didn't believe them because I thought it was a long way off.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的人已经这样说了一段时间了，但我没相信他们，因为我以为那还很遥远。

sentences.en: What's happened to me is understanding there might be a big difference between this kind of intelligence and biological intelligence has made me completely revise my opinions.
sentences.zh: 发生在我身上的是，我意识到这种智能与生物智能之间可能存在巨大差异，这让我彻底修正了自己的观点。

sentences.en: It's a complicated situation for him to be in.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这是一个复杂的情况。

sentences.en: Again, do you regret your role in all this?
sentences.zh: 再次问你，你后悔自己在这一切中所扮演的角色吗？

sentences.en: So the question is, looking back 50 years,
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，回顾50年前，

sentences.en: would I have done something different?
sentences.zh: 我会做些不同的事情吗？

sentences.en: Given the choices I made 50 years ago, I think there were reasonable choices to make.
sentences.zh: 鉴于我50年前做出的选择，我认为那是合理的选择。

sentences.en: It's just turned out very recently
sentences.zh: 只是最近才发现

sentences.en: that this is going somewhere I didn't expect.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到事情的发展超出了我的预期。

sentences.en: And so I regret the fact that it's as advanced as it is now on my part in doing that.
sentences.zh: 所以我很后悔，因为就我个人而言，它现在已经发展到这种地步了。

sentences.en: But it's a distinction
sentences.zh: 但这是一种区别，

sentences.en: Bertrand Russell made between wise decisions and fortunate decisions.
sentences.zh: 伯特兰·罗素在明智的决定和幸运的决定之间所做的区分。

sentences.en: He paraphrased the British philosopher
sentences.zh: 他转述了英国哲学家

sentences.en: Bertrand Russell.
sentences.zh: 伯特兰·罗素的话。

sentences.en: You can make a wise decision that turns out to be unfortunate.
sentences.zh: 你可以做出一个明智的决定，但结果却是不幸的。

sentences.en: Saying that you can make a wise decision that still turns out to be unfortunate.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你可能做出了明智的决定，但最终结果却不尽如人意。

sentences.en: And that's basically how he feels.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是他的感受。

sentences.en: And I think it was a wise decision to try and figure out how the brain worked.
sentences.zh: 我认为试图弄清楚大脑是如何运作的，是一个明智的决定。

sentences.en: And part of my motivation was to make human society more sensible.
sentences.zh: 我当初的部分动机是想让社会变得更理智。

sentences.en: But it turns out that maybe it was unfortunate.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这可能是不幸的。

sentences.en: It's reminding me, Cade, of Andrei Sakharov, who was, of course, the Soviet scientist who invented the hydrogen bomb and witnessed his invention.
sentences.zh: 凯德，这让我想起了安德烈·萨哈罗夫，他当然是发明了氢弹并亲眼目睹了自己发明成果的苏联科学家。

sentences.en: And became horrified and spent the rest of his life trying to fight against it.
sentences.zh: 他感到非常惊恐，余生都在努力与之抗争。

sentences.en: Do you see him that way?
sentences.zh: 你也是这样看他的吗？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's someone who has helped build a powerful technology and now he is extremely concerned about the consequences.
sentences.zh: 他帮助创造了一种强大的技术，现在他对自己所造成的后果感到极其担忧。

sentences.en: Even if you think the doomsday scenario is ridiculous or implausible, there are so many other possible outcomes that Jeff points to.
sentences.zh: 即使你认为世界末日的设想是荒谬或不可信的，杰夫指出的其他许多可能的结果也依然存在。

sentences.en: And that is reason enough to be concerned.
sentences.zh: 这本身就足以让人担忧了。

sentences.en: Cade, thank you for coming on the show.
sentences.zh: 凯德，感谢你来到我们的节目。

sentences.en: Glad to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。
